title: Reward models, the KL-optimal policy, and DPO
brief: Implement the Bradley-Terry reward loss and the DPO loss it becomes after substituting in the KL-regularised optimum, and watch DPO's gradient sharpen a policy's preferences.
hints: bradley_terry_loss is the mean of -log(sigmoid(reward_chosen - reward_rejected)). Write your own numerically stable sigmoid: for z < 0, exp(z) / (1 + exp(z)) avoids overflow that 1 / (1 + exp(-z)) would hit.

The gradient of the mean Bradley-Terry loss with respect to reward_chosen is (sigmoid(z) - 1) / n, and the gradient with respect to reward_rejected is the negative of that, since the loss depends only on the difference z = reward_chosen - reward_rejected.

optimal_policy computes logits = ref_logprobs + rewards / beta, subtracts the row-wise max before exponentiating for stability, then normalises along the last axis. That subtraction does not change the normalised result.

dpo_loss is bradley_terry_loss applied to implicit_reward(policy_chosen_logps, ref_chosen_logps, beta) and implicit_reward(policy_rejected_logps, ref_rejected_logps, beta). Writing it that way makes dpo_grad reuse the same derivative you already worked out for bradley_terry_grad.
implicit_reward is just beta * (policy_logps - ref_logps), elementwise, for whatever shape you are given.
